messages:
bryan: linkcheck spammed errors for /api/auth - several anchor lookups 404. page renders fine locally but mkdocs build shows missing fragment ids.

nora: I noticed the rendered HTML had H2s but the id attributes were missing. happened after Sam's PR that added an HTML comment above a heading.

bryan: example snippet from the md: `<!-- TODO: revisit this section -->
## Authentication flow` — looks harmless but apparently mkdocs' markdown-it plugin treats HTML comments as block-level nodes and stops the slugger from attaching IDs in some cases.

nora: wild. so heading is produced but slugger not run? this breaks any inbound links like /api/auth#authentication-flow. linkcheck flags them.

link-bot: linkcheck: /api/auth#authentication-flow -> 404 (anchor not found)

bryan: quick fix is to move comments to above the blank line or convert to an HTML-safe remark comment: `<!--- -->`? better: use a markdown comment pattern `<!--- TODO ->`? not ideal.

nora: safer fix: adjust the build plugin order. If we run the slugger after the html parser, it re-applies IDs. I tried patching mkdocs.yml to ensure `markdown_extensions: - toc: permalink: false` and explicit `slugify: true` but still inconsistent.

bryan: opened a small PR that strips HTML comments before rendering for headings only: scripts/strip_heading_comments.py and wired it into the docs build pipeline. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4307

ci-bot: build #3201 triggered by bryan/strip-heading-comments

link-bot: after applying strip, anchor present: /api/auth#authentication-flow -> 200

nora: I ran the patched build locally, linkcheck passes for the page. we should add a unit test: create a test md file with an HTML comment above a bunch of headings and assert generated HTML contains ids.

bryan: added test and a changelog note for docs maintainers. also posted in the docs runbook that authors should avoid inline HTML comments directly above headings.

ci-bot: build #3201 passed. merge allowed.

bryan: merged. pinging @sam to nudge if they want to rebase their PRs where they touched headings.

nora: follow-up: file a tracker to audit other plugins that mutate AST ordering; might be a problem with other edge-case markdown constructs.

bryan: filed issue #783: "Heading ID loss when HTML comments precede headings". adding to sprint backlog.

link-bot: linkcheck run on main after deploy shows no regressions.

bryan: closing thread. thanks for quick turnaround.
